# N-mixture (abundance) models for saproxylic beetles

This code analyzes abudance data for the saproxylic beetle *Plagionotus detritus* collected in the Iron Gates Natural Park, Romania and published in Brodie et al. 2019.

Brodie, B. S., V. D. Popescu, R. Iosif, et al. 2019. Non-lethal monitoring of longicorn beetle communities using generic pheromone lures and occupancy models. Ecological Indicators 101:330-340.


# DATA SETUP

Set working directory, read data from a .csv file and examine the data structure; add the two R packages used by this analysis: *unmarked* for N-mixture analyses and *MuMIn* for multi-model inference

```{r}
library(unmarked)
library(MuMIn)

beetles <- read.csv("data/Pdet_dataset.csv")
names(beetles)
attach(beetles)
str(beetles)
```

Setup *unmarked* dataframe using site-specific and survey-specific covariates survey-specific covariates are: JulianDay (day of year) and Precipitation; site-specific covariates are  Ground cover and Average tree diameter

Create survey-specific covariates and standardize them

```{r}
JulianDay = matrix(cbind(Julian1, Julian2, Julian3, Julian4,
                         Julian5, Julian6, Julian7, Julian8,
                         Julian9, Julian10, Julian11, Julian12))
JulianDay = matrix(scale(JulianDay), nrow=50, byrow=F)

Precipitation = matrix(cbind(Precip1, Precip2, Precip3, Precip4,
                             Precip5, Precip6, Precip7, Precip8,
                             Precip9, Precip10, Precip11, Precip12))
Precipitation = matrix(scale(Precipitation), nrow=50, byrow=F)
```

Create an *unmarked* object for our focal species, Plagionotus detritus.
Create an R object that can be read by the 'unmarked' package. The object contains 3 types of data:
  1) detection/nondetection data (the observations grouped into a matrix "y")
  2) site-level covariates; these can be any variables that do not vary with survey occasion,
             such as landscape characteristics, habitat types, site characteristics etc.
            - these variables are used to model ABUNDANCE; they can also be used to model DETECTION
  3) observation-level covariates; these can be any variables recorded at the time of survey
             that may influence detection
             - these variables are used to model DETECTION

```{r}
PdetUMF <- with(beetles, {
  unmarkedFramePCount(
    y = cbind(Pdet1, Pdet2, Pdet3, Pdet4, Pdet5, Pdet6, Pdet7, 
              Pdet8, Pdet9, Pdet10, Pdet11, Pdet12),
    siteCovs = data.frame(scale(GroundCover), scale(AvgDiameter)),
    obsCovs = list(Julian = JulianDay,
                   Precip = Precipitation))
  
})

plot(PdetUMF)
```

Count data can follow Poisson or Negative Binomial distributions; if there are a lot of zeroes in the data, count data can also follow a Zero-Inflated Poisson distribution; as such, the first step is to parameterize a model with haphazardly selected variables and test which type of distribution fits the data best.

For simplicity, wil will only use 2 site-level variables in this exercise: Average tree diameter and Ground cover

```{r}
mP <- pcount(~Julian+Precip ~scale.AvgDiameter. + scale.GroundCover., 
             mixture="P", K=100, data=PdetUMF) # Poisson distribution "P"
mNB <- pcount(~Julian+Precip ~scale.AvgDiameter. + scale.GroundCover., 
              mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF) # negative binomial "NB"
mZIP <- pcount(~Julian+Precip ~scale.AvgDiameter. + scale.GroundCover., 
              mixture="ZIP", K=100, data=PdetUMF) # zero-inflated Poisson "ZIP"

# model selection using AICc
modelList <- fitList("modP" = mP, "modNB" = mNB, "modZIP" = mZIP)
modSel_Pdet <- modSel(modelList)
modSel_Pdet
```

The distribution that fits the data best is Negative Binomial and will continue using this distribution for th erest of the analysis.

The analysis has 2 stages: First we need to evaluate the best predictors for detection. Therefore, we run several models that contains the same suite of site-related variables (for modeling abundance), but various combinations of survey-specific variables for modeling detection. The goal is to identify the best variables that explain detection probability, when then use them in the next step of the analysis.   

# BUILD AND RUN DETECTION MODELS (using a full model for abundance)

Run several models for detection; the goal is to compare models with different parameterizations for detection using the same vaiables for abundance across models. The function is *pcount* and contains 2 sub-models: the first "~" is the detection submodel; the seond "~" is the abundance submodel.   

```{r}
m0 <- pcount(~1 ~scale.AvgDiameter.+ scale.GroundCover., mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF)
m1 <- pcount(~Julian ~scale.AvgDiameter.+ scale.GroundCover., mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF)
m2 <- pcount(~Precip ~scale.AvgDiameter.+ scale.GroundCover., mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF)
m3 <- pcount(~Julian+Precip ~scale.AvgDiameter.+ scale.GroundCover., mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF)

# detection model selection using AICc
modelList <- fitList(Null = m0, "mod1" = m1, "mod2" = m2, "mod3" = m3)
modSel_Pdet <- modSel(modelList, nullmod = 'Null')
modSel_Pdet
```

Model 3, which includes both precipitation and Julain day performs best, and we will use these 2 variables in the next step

# BUILD AND RUN MODELS FOR ABUNDANCE

We now run several models that include different variables explaining abundance and the best detection variable(s) identified above. We are only running a small set of models here, but one can build and run many more models based on a priori hypotheses, exppert knowledge about limiting and favorable factors, etc. 

```{r}
Pdet_Null <- pcount(~Julian+Precip  ~1, mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF)
Pdet_m0 <- pcount(~Julian+Precip  ~scale.GroundCover., mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF) 
Pdet_m1 <- pcount(~Julian+Precip  ~scale.AvgDiameter., mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF)
Pdet_m2 <- pcount(~Julian+Precip  ~scale.AvgDiameter. + scale.GroundCover., 
                  mixture="NB", K=100, data=PdetUMF) 

# model selection using AICc 
modelList_Pdet <- fitList(Null = Pdet_Null, m0 = Pdet_m0, m1 = Pdet_m1, m2 = Pdet_m2)
modSel_Pdet <- modSel(modelList_Pdet, nullmod = 'Null')
modSel_Pdet
```

The best model only contains Ground Cover as a predictor for beetle abundance. Next, we compute model predictions and estimates of abundance and detection for the species of interest.

```{r}
# extract coeficients for best model
summary(Pdet_m0)
coef(Pdet_m0)
```

```{r}
# estimate individuals per site from the best model
Pdet_abund <- predict(Pdet_m0, type="state")
Pdet_abund # predicted abundance at each trap location 
mean(Pdet_abund$Predicted) # mean predicted abundance across all traps
```

```{r}
# compute overall abundance estimates
lcab <- linearComb(Pdet_m0, c(1, 1), type="state")
lcab <- backTransform(lcab)
lcab
```

```{r}
# estimate probability of detection from the best model
Pdet_det <- predict(Pdet_m0, type="det")
head(Pdet_det)
mean(Pdet_det$Predicted)
```

```{r}
# compute overall detection estimates
lcdet <- linearComb(Pdet_m0, c(1, 1, 1), type="det")
lcdet <- backTransform(lcdet)
lcdet
``` 

# PLOT RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN VARIABLES AND DETECTION PROBABILITY

To plot these relationships, we first create a new data frame for prediction with the  variable of interest ranging from min to max values, while keeping all the other variables in the model at their mean value.

```{r}
# predictions for date
Date_grid <- seq(min(PdetUMF@obsCovs$Julian), 
                 max(PdetUMF@obsCovs$Julian), 
                 length = 50)
grid <- expand.grid(Julian = Date_grid, Precip = mean(PdetUMF@obsCovs$Precip))
Date_pred <- predict(Pdet_m0, type = "det", as.data.frame(grid))
str(Date_pred)

plot(Date_grid,
     Date_pred$Predicted, 
     type = "l", 
     lwd = 3,
     ylim = c(0,0.3),
     xlab = "scaled Julian Date", 
     ylab = "Detection probability")
lines(Date_grid, Date_pred$lower)
lines(Date_grid, Date_pred$upper)
```

```{r}
# predictions for precipitation
Precip_grid <- seq(min(PdetUMF@obsCovs$Precip), 
                max(PdetUMF@obsCovs$Precip), 
                length = 50)
grid <- expand.grid(Julian = mean(PdetUMF@obsCovs$Julian), Precip = Precip_grid)
Precip_pred <- predict(Pdet_m0, type = "det", as.data.frame(grid))
str(Precip_pred)

plot(Precip_grid,
     Precip_pred$Predicted, 
     type = "l", 
     lwd = 3, 
     ylim = c(0,0.3),
     xlab = "scaled Precipitation", 
     ylab = "Detection probability")
lines(Precip_grid, Precip_pred$lower)
lines(Precip_grid, Precip_pred$upper)
```

# PLOT RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN VARIABLE Ground Cover AND ABUNDANCE

```{r}
GC_grid <- seq(min(PdetUMF@siteCovs$scale.GroundCover.), 
               max(PdetUMF@siteCovs$scale.GroundCover.), 
               length = 50)
scale.GroundCover. <- GC_grid
GC_pred <- predict(Pdet_m0, type = "state", as.data.frame(GC_grid))
str(GC_pred)

plot(GC_grid,
     GC_pred$Predicted,
     type = "l", 
     lwd = 3,
     xlab = "scaled Ground Cover", 
     ylab = "Beetle abundance")

lines(GC_grid, GC_pred$lower)
lines(GC_grid, GC_pred$upper)
```
